explanation: Brand was hunting for the philosopher's stone. His waxy discovery glowed in the dark, so it was named from the Greek for 'light-bearer'.

claims.text: Hennig Brand discovered phosphorus in 1669 by boiling down urine.
Sulfur and arsenic were known long before 1669, and nitrogen was discovered only in the 1770s.
Brand was searching for the philosopher's stone when he found phosphorus.
White phosphorus is waxy and glows in the dark when exposed to air.
The name phosphorus comes from the Greek for 'light-bearer'.
